section_summary: This concluding section of decimal file 894.00 (File 997, part 2) contains records of the American Embassy in Tokyo for December 1937 and January 1938. It includes schedules of telegrams and despatches sent to the Department of State throughout December 1937 and Despatch No. 2735 of January 18, 1938, transmitting Embassy Report No. 135 on conditions in Japan. The extensive monthly report documents the international crisis precipitated by the Japanese bombing and sinking of the U.S.S. Panay and attacks on British naval vessels on the Yangtze River, along with the fall of Nanking, Japanese-sponsored autonomous regimes in occupied China, diplomatic disputes over Manchurian extraterritoriality and Chinese customs, and domestic political suppression and wartime economic controls in Japan.

subfiles.about: Continuation of a schedule of telegrams and despatches sent by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State during December 1937.
subfiles.summary: This document continues the monthly record of official communications transmitted from the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State during December 1937. It lists telegrams numbered 612 through 700 (dated December 10 to December 31) and despatches numbered 2682 through 2712 (dated December 2 to December 31), recording the serial number, transmission date, and subject of each communication. Prominent subjects include the sinking of the U.S.S. Panay, Japanese attacks on the British gunboats Ladybird and Bee, the administration of the Shanghai customs, Alaskan salmon fisheries, and Embassy personnel matters.
subfiles.title: Telegrams and Despatches Sent to the Department During December 1937 [Continuation]

subfiles.about: Diplomatic cover despatch and attached monthly political report from Ambassador Joseph C. Grew reviewing political, military, diplomatic, and economic conditions in Japan during December 1937.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits Embassy Report No. 135 reviewing political, military, diplomatic, and economic developments in Japan during December 1937. The report covers the diplomatic crisis resulting from the Japanese bombing and sinking of the U.S.S. Panay and attacks on British warships Ladybird and Bee on the Yangtze River, detailing American and British protests, Japanese official apologies, indemnifications, and diplomatic settlements. It also recounts Japanese military operations in China, including the capture of Nanking, fighting in Shantung, aerial bombings, and the establishment of Japanese-sponsored autonomous regimes in Peiping, Nanking, and Mongolia. In addition, it examines Japanese relations with the Soviet Union, Italy, Germany, and France, extraterritoriality disputes in Manchuria, domestic Cabinet changes under Home Minister Suetsugu, political party suppression, the opening of the 73rd Diet, and tightening foreign exchange regulations.
subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 2735: Report on Conditions in Japan During the Month of December, 1937 (Report No. 135)

subfiles.about: Complete schedule of telegrams and despatches sent by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State during December 1937.
subfiles.summary: This document provides a complete chronological list of telegrams numbered 584 through 700 (December 1 to December 31) and despatches numbered 2682 through 2712 (December 2 to December 31) sent by the American Embassy in Tokyo to the Department of State during December 1937. Each entry records the communication number, date, and subject matter. Major subjects include the Panay crisis, the Japanese advance on Nanking and Shanghai, maritime incidents on the Yangtze River, protection of American nationals and property in China, Alaskan fisheries controversies, and routine Embassy administrative business.
subfiles.title: Telegrams and Despatches Sent to the Department During December 1937
